facts.fact: The IMPULSE study (Journal of Global Health 2025) found that 21.4% of the 14 health facilities it assessed in the Central African Republic used a functional electronic system for routine data entry and analysis, against over 75% in Ethiopia, Tanzania and Uganda; the 14 were hospitals and health centres giving emergency obstetric care in Bangui and health regions 1, 2 and 7, chosen for access and security, with data collected between November 2022 and July 2024.

The IMPULSE study found a functional electronic system for data entry and analysis in 83.3% of the 6 district health offices it assessed in the Central African Republic, against 21.4% of the 14 facilities, and states that all data offices used DHIS2 for key data analysis; data collected between November 2022 and July 2024.

systems.tiers: district health offices (all assessed data offices used it for key data analysis); 21.4% of 14 assessed facilities used an electronic system, not named
